concerns.text: FR-013 lacks an explicit reference to any User Story; it is currently an orphaned functional requirement.

FR-013 states the system MUST issue a warning **and halt downstream analyses** if a cohort fails the sample‑size requirement, whereas the Edge Cases section says the pipeline will only issue a warning and suggest additional data collection (implying continuation). This contradictory handling of insufficient power creates an internal inconsistency between functional requirements and edge‑case behavior.

FR-012 specifies a power analysis for detecting a standardized effect size β = 0.1 with 80 % power at α = 0.05, but does not identify the statistical model (e.g., correlation, regression, t‑test) or the appropriate power‑analysis method. Without this detail the requirement is ambiguous and cannot be deterministically verified.

The specification’s Success Criteria (SC‑001‑SC‑007) list only tables and numeric summaries; the original idea explicitly calls for visualizations (volcano plots, CLR‑based ordination) in the “Output generation” section. No requirement or test case for generating these figures is present, constituting an under‑reach of the idea’s deliverables.

FR‑012 introduces an a‑priori power analysis (detect β = 0.1 with 80 % power) and associated warning/halt logic. The idea’s methodology sketch never mentions a power analysis; this adds a new analytical step that was not requested, representing an over‑reach beyond the original research question.

FR-012 specifies an a priori power analysis using a two‑sample t‑test framework (e.g., statsmodels.stats.power.TTestIndPower) to detect a standardized effect size β = 0.1 for the primary association tests, which are Spearman correlations on CLR‑transformed data and MaAsLin2 linear models. A t‑test power calculation is not appropriate for these statistical models, making the power analysis method mismatched to the hypothesis tests and potentially leading to incorrect sample‑size requirements.
